correctness.rationale: For each real atomless finite measure, each finite-dimensional kernel, every fixed f and every Rademacher-type sign sequence, the pointwise limit of ||r_n f-z|| is int max(|f|,|z|). Finite-dimensional compactness of approximate norm-minimizing kernel vectors justifies passage to the infimum and gives the exact distance ||f||. A minimum-norm representative of each unit coset exists and its sign perturbations are weakly null; plus/minus estimates and weak lower semicontinuity prove WASQ for the quotient. This requires neither any metric-graph model nor a numerical experiment.

originality.rationale: PASS is confined to the universal finite-dimensional quotient theorem and exact Rademacher distance law. The first (2022) primary arXiv version of Kaasik--Veeorg explicitly asserted geodesic free spaces are WASQ (Theorem 3.1), which would imply the graph corollary, although the revised (2023) version narrows this to finite-support vectors. No priority is claimed for graph WASQ. Neither version asserts the new quotient law, and the 2023 atomless L1 WASQ paper supplies only a lemma for ambient L1 before quotienting. Queries for equivalent quotient norm-distance formulations found no covering literature.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent finite-dimensional L1 quotient permanence theorem or exact Rademacher distance identity may exist in unindexed earlier literature.

value.rationale: A structural permanence theorem for WASQ under **every finite-dimensional norm quotient** of a nonzero real atomless L1, together with a uniform sharp asymptotic distance law for all sign oscillations and every kernel. This pinpoints the compactness obstruction in norm-quotient geometry. Finite compact metric graphs motivate this question via finite-dimensional cycle-flow kernels, although their WASQ property was asserted in the earlier v1 geodesic literature and is not treated as a priority claim.
